newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PARLIAMENT ADOPT CONTROVERSIAL TAX BILL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PARLIAMENT ADOPT CONTROVERSIAL TAX BILL.

text.p: Polish legislators on Thursday adopted a bill standardising all taxes to eliminate legal loopholes and curb tax evasion, which includes a constroversial clause obliging those better-off to declare their wealth.

The bill, known as the tax ordination, does not determine tax levels, but provides a unifying legal basis for all taxes, which the government says should bring Poland's law to the European Union standards.

Under the draft law, passed by the lower house of parliament in a 266 to 84 vote with 11 abstentions, a single adult who has more than 500,000 zlotys in assets, securities or cash will have to declare them each year to enable the tax office to determine if taxes have been paid properly.

The bill's critics, mainly business groups and some opposition parties, say it would give the state too much power over citizens and did not incluce enough measures preventing officials from abusing it.

The bill, which still has to clear the senate and be signed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski, would in some cases give tax inspectors powers to glean into people's accounts at banks, brokerages and investment funds.

The draft, which would take effect next year unless the senate fails to pass it before parliamentary polls on September 21, would allow the Finance Ministry to speed up tax deductions or reimbursements, also in the case of value added tax.
